doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Serge Chaloff and the Band Box front line
summary: Terry props up addicted saxophonists Chaloff and Rouse on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Serge Chaloff, right. Serge Chaloff and Rouse and Buddy DeFranco and I were the front line in Basie’s band when we played the Band Box in New York. Serge was a junkie, and Rouse was messed up, so Buddy DeFranco’s out front, playing a solo, and the rhythm section’s back there, Basie and Jimmy Lewis, Freddie Green, and Gus Johnson, pumping away, and I’m playing in the background [Terry sings a riff], and I’m holding up both of them with elbows. I got an elbow over here holding up Rouse, an elbow holding up Serge Chaloff. They’re trying to play and swing.
Serge was a marvelous musician, fantastic baritone saxophone player. His mother was a teacher, so he had a natural – naturally he was marvelous player. But he was a victim, a real pitiful victim.
